title: veyq-subtree manifest
description: The manifest of a veyq node-subtree download (ADR 0082): the plaintext tree of one node and everything under it. Version 2 (written today) sits at `.veyq/manifest.json` beside the tree, which the store-only ZIP holds as itself: a directory per node that holds others, each file under its own name, every name made safe for every file system. Version 1 (still read, never written) sat at `manifest.json` with every payload under `data/<node id>/`. Core owns the envelope and the node shape; each kind owns the shape of its `content` (the `$defs` below document Depot's and Memories'). Readers ignore unknown fields and refuse a `version` newer than they know. Beyond what JSON Schema can say, a reader caps the tree at 200000 nodes and a depth of 100, the manifest at 128 MiB, and refuses a payload path that does not lie at or under its node's `path`.

version.description: Format version. Bumped only by a change an older reader would misread; an additive field never bumps it. 2: the tree layout with `.veyq/manifest.json` (ADR 0082 decision 3). 1: the `data/<id>/` layout, read for archives written before it.

exportedAt.description: Client clock at export, RFC 3339 UTC.

appVersion.description: The exporting web client's release identity (informational).

options.description: Version 1 only: the options chosen at export. A version 2 writer omits it (there are no options) and a reader ignores it.

includeLocation.description: False when GPS and place data were left out of the manifest at export time; the fields are then absent, not null.

applications.description: Version 2: every application whose kinds the tree carries, with the version of its content schema the writer wrote. A reader lists, before it writes anything, the nodes of an application it does not have and of one whose content is newer than it reads (ADR 0082 decision 9). Each `id` appears once.

id.description: The application's id: the part of a `content.type` before the dot (`depot`, `memories`).

contentSchema.description: The highest `content.schema` of this application's kinds in the tree.

archivePath.description: Version 2: a path inside the ZIP, relative, `/`-separated, the node's place in the tree (`Trip 2025/Lisbon/IMG_0412.jpg`). Every segment is a safe archive name (ADR 0082 decision 3: no `/` or `\`, not `.` or `..`, no control character, no Windows reserved name, no trailing dot or space, bounded, clashes numbered `Name (2)`), and nothing lies under `.veyq/`, which holds the manifest. A label, never an identity: the manifest, not the path, says which node a payload belongs to.

archivePathV1.description: Version 1: `data/<node.id>/<file name>`. The importer reads only paths it finds in the manifest and refuses any that leaves data/ (no `..`, no absolute path, no backslash).

path.description: Where the bytes are: an `archivePath` in version 2, an `archivePathV1` in version 1.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the stored bytes; the importer verifies it while streaming.

modifiedAt.description: Optional, Depot: the file's modified time at export, in milliseconds since the epoch; restored on import.

id.description: Archive-local id, unique in this manifest (`n1`, `n2`, ...). Not a veyq node id; carries no meaning outside the file.

kind.description: The node kind (FOLDER, FILE, DEPOT_DROPBOX, MEMORY, CHAPTER, ...). An importing build that lacks the kind skips that node and its subtree and reports it.

name.description: The node's name as veyq shows it. Its archive path's last segment is this name made safe, so the two may differ.

path.description: Version 2: where the node sits in the archive. A node that holds others (a folder, a Memory, a chapter) is a directory and its payloads lie in it; a node of a kind that IS one file (a Depot file) is that file, its one payload at this very path. The exported node's own path is its safe name. Required in version 2.

cover.description: The node's cover image (core's COVER attachment), if any.

metadata.description: The kind's plaintext node metadata that is not content (e.g. a Memory's description). Open: unknown keys are ignored.

content.description: What the kind's export hook supplied; absent for a node that has none (a FOLDER).

children.description: In the order the source tree showed them.

type.description: `<application>.<name>`; the importing kind's hook dispatches on it, and its application part names the entry of `applications`.

schema.description: The kind's own content schema version; the hook refuses a newer one.

depotFile.description: Depot: the one blob of a FILE node. The file's name is the node's name.

depotDropBox.description: Depot: a DEPOT_DROPBOX node. It carries nothing but what it was: its guests' folders are its FOLDER children (each under the name the drop box shows it by, a repeated name numbered), their files theirs. An importing build creates it as a plain FOLDER - a drop key, guests' identities and links cannot be rebuilt from a download.

memoriesMemory.description: Memories: the content of a MEMORY node. Its chapters are the node's CHAPTER children, each with its own `memories.chapter` content; the media listed here are the Memory's own.

participants.description: Who was there, as display names (text only): ids mean nothing in another instance, so an import never restores them (ADR 0083).

file.description: The pristine original, never a derivative.

capturedAt.description: The capture time as the Memory shows it (EXIF, the file's time, or the member's correction).

location.description: Informational: an import re-reads the coordinate from the file's own EXIF (there is no way to seal one the file lacks) and restores only `place`. Version 1 left it out when `options.includeLocation` was false.

place.description: The place name the Memory shows.

exif.description: Camera EXIF the original carries, as read; open. Version 1 left out the locating tags when `options.includeLocation` was false.

contributor.description: Text only: who added the medium ("Anna"). Not an identity; an import never maps it to a member.

capturedAtCorrected.description: Present when the member had corrected the capture time (an override); an import restores it as one.

memoriesChapter.description: Memories: the content of a CHAPTER node - the same fields as a Memory's (media, date, place, cover, participants).

memoriesPlace.description: The Memory's place as it is sealed in the node's metadata (name, how it was named, whether its position is derived from the media or fixed). Version 1 left it out when `options.includeLocation` was false.

memoriesCover.description: The cover: one of the exported media (by its index in `media`) or an uploaded image (a payload), framed by a normalized 0..1 crop.

nodeV1.description: A version 1 node: the common shape, every child a version 1 node.

nodeV2.description: A version 2 node: the common shape plus its `path`, every child a version 2 node.
